main_text.p: quæ singulæ adulteram aggressæ miseram crudeli morte dilaniarunt. Auentinus id factum esse scripsit sub duce Bauariæ Hum- berto , in pago quodam Bauarico nomine Thengen/in quo frequentia fuerint adulte- ria : additque hanc ciconiam adulteram coa- &tam fuisse solam educare & pascere pullos exclufos , mare opetam ipsi suam negante, hunc vero sub illud tempus, quo à nobis in alias migrare terras ciconiæ solent , venisse comitatum agmine ciconiarum , à quibus adultera confixa & dicerpta fit.

OccidisseAd extremum honos ciconiis in Thessa- ciconiamlia tantus,vt capitale sit occidisse, eademque in Thessalegibus pœna,quæ in homicidam, tefte Plin. lib.10.cap.23. In ea namque regione tan- lia capi- tale esttàm aiunt serpentum prouenire vim, vt,nisi à ciconiis conficerentur , incolas pellerent.

Ciconia futuraPræsensionum quoque quandam vim inesse ciconiis testatur Alexander ab Alexandria, prefen- tiuntAnnoenimà Christi natiuitate 454.cum At- tila Aquileiam obsideret, ciconias animad- uertit , quæ in turribus ciuitatis nidificaue- rant,vno impetu ex vrbe migrare,atque suos fœtus exportare, vnde milites hoc aufpicio exhortatus tanquam vrbem interitui proxi- Ciconia- rum pru-mam ciconiæ deferrent, vrbem cepit. Pru- dentiadentia denique ciconiarum ex eo apparet, quod ante abitum vno in loco cögregentur, consilia quasi publica de abitione ineuntes

page.notes: Marginal notes in the left margin are catchword-like and partly cut off; "lia capi- tale e?" is read as "tale est" with the last letters doubtful. The reference "454" is doubtful. The initial word of the second line of the first paragraph, "&tum" (factum), has an unusual ligature and is doubtful. The top-left "Thengen/in" has a decorated initial T, read as T. The marginal note "dentia" and the "&c" at the lower right are uncertain as to placement.
